resolutions.researcher_notes: The Journal Record (Oklahoma City business paper, live, one of the wiki's own seed citations), May 4, 2018: describes Enable Midstream's 'Wildcat pipeline project' as under active construction with photo of pipe being laid, and quotes Enable's own spokesman on the project's commercial in-service plan. Continental Resources, Inc. 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (Q1 2018 earnings release, filed 2018-05-03 with SEC): 'Project Wildcat: 400 MMcfd of Firm Transportation from SCOOP and STACK ... First Flow Starting in June 2018 ... Project Wildcat is expected to be fully in service in July 2018.' Two distinct publishers (an independent Oklahoma newspaper and the anchor-shipper company's own SEC filing, neither of which is Enable itself) agreeing the pipeline was under construction/entering service in mid-2018 and is a live, in-service natural gas pipeline -- supports the sheet's Status=operating (this is a 2026 sweep of a line that entered service in 2018 with no reported shutdown). tier=high, independent=true.

Journal Record: 'a natural gas pipeline that connects Oklahoma to the Dallas-Fort Worth area.' Enable Midstream Partners, LP 10-Q for Q1 2017 (filed 2017-05-03 with SEC): 'Project Wildcat rich gas takeaway solution -- The Partnership has entered into an agreement to deliver approximately 400 MMcf/d of rich natural gas from the Anadarko Basin.' Two distinct publishers (independent newspaper + the pipeline owner's own SEC filing) both explicitly describe the commodity as natural gas, matching Fuel=Gas. tier=high, independent=true.

Enable Midstream Partners, LP's 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017, filed with the SEC on 2017-05-03, already describes Project Wildcat in its 'Commercial and Construction Update' as an EXISTING agreement ('The Partnership has entered into an agreement to deliver approximately 400 MMcf/d...'), i.e. the commercial commitment/proposal was already in place by the time of this May 2017 filing -- matching the sheet's ProposalYear=2017 / ProposalMonth=May exactly (this filing date is very likely the wiki's own original source for that month/year pairing). Single publisher (Enable itself, the pipeline's developer/owner), so tier=medium/independent=false -- I could not find a second, distinct-publisher source independently dating the announcement to May 2017 specifically (Continental Resources' and Journal Record's coverage are both from May 2018, a year later, and describe the anchor-shipper agreement/construction milestone, not the original 2017 proposal). Checked and ruled out: the wiki's EIA seed citation (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php) is a bare navigation/data-portal page, not a deep link to any specific document -- not usable as a citation per the hard rule against citing navigation surfaces; the wiki's RBN Energy seed citation is a Google Images search-results URL, not an article -- also not citable, and I could not locate the underlying RBN Energy article ('Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough') directly (rbnenergy.com returned 403 on the guessed URL, no Wayback capture found for that slug, and WebSearch quota was already exhausted for this session).

Continental Resources, Inc. 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (filed 2018-05-03): 'Project Wildcat: 400 MMcfd of Firm Transportation from SCOOP and STACK ... First Flow Starting in June 2018' and, in the body text, 'Project Wildcat is expected to be fully in service in July 2018.' Enable Midstream Partners' own Q1 2017 10-Q separately projected the project 'to be in service by the end of the second quarter of 2018.' Two distinct publishers (the anchor shipper, Continental Resources, and the pipeline owner, Enable Midstream Partners) both place first flow / full in-service within calendar-year 2018 (June-July), matching the sheet's StartYear1=2018. tier=high, independent=true. Note the two sources differ by about a month on the exact month (June first-flow vs. July fully-in-service vs. 'end of Q2' projection) -- all land within the same year, which is the only value staged (StartMonth1 is blank on the sheet), so this is not a conflict worth flagging.

Three distinct publishers state the identical figure verbatim: Journal Record -- 'Continental has committed to paying for 400 million cubic feet per day of natural gas capacity in Enable's Wildcat line'; Continental Resources 8-K -- 'Project Wildcat: 400 MMcfd of Firm Transportation from SCOOP and STACK'; Enable Midstream Partners' own 10-Q -- 'an agreement to deliver approximately 400 MMcf/d of rich natural gas.' All three exactly match the sheet's Capacity=400.00 MMcf/d. tier=high, independent=true (an independent newspaper + the shipper's own SEC filing + the owner's own SEC filing -- at least two of the three are mutually independent of each other, satisfying the >=2-distinct-publisher bar).

Journal Record: 'Enable saw a 25-percent increase in natural gas volume gathered since early 2016 from the Anadarko Basin, which includes both the SCOOP and STACK plays' -- Wildcat is described throughout the article as the takeaway solution for this Anadarko Basin (SCOOP/STACK) production. Enable's own 10-Q: 'deliver approximately 400 MMcf/d of rich natural gas from the Anadarko Basin to north Texas.' Two distinct publishers agree the gas is sourced from the Anadarko Basin, matching FuelSource=Anadarko Basin exactly. tier=high, independent=true.

The pipeline's delivery/end point is well corroborated in Texas: Journal Record -- 'connect Oklahoma oil and gas fields to the Tolar Hub in Johnson County, Texas'; Enable's own 10-Q -- 'access to the Texas intrastate natural gas markets, including the Tolar Hub, by contracting ... for 400 MMcf/d of firm processing capacity at the Godley Plant in Johnson County, Texas.' This directly supports EndState/Province=Texas, EndCountryOrArea=United States. CONCERN (do not change the value; flagging for Update): both of these same sources describe the pipeline's ORIGIN as Oklahoma, not Texas -- Journal Record's photo caption reads 'Construction workers put pipes in place for Enable Midstream Partners' Wildcat pipeline project, which crosses Grady County' (Grady County is in Oklahoma, part of the SCOOP/STACK play), and the article's lede is 'a natural gas pipeline that connects Oklahoma to the Dallas-Fort Worth area'; Enable's 10-Q likewise: 'deliver ... rich natural gas from the Anadarko Basin [Oklahoma] to north Texas.' Neither source places any part of the pipeline's route or gathering origin in Texas apart from its Johnson County, Texas terminus. The sheet currently has BOTH StartState/Province=Texas and EndState/Province=Texas -- on this evidence StartState/Province more likely belongs in Oklahoma (StartCountryOrArea would remain United States either way). Re-checked: no other unit in this brief or in the wiki seed citations pool contradicts this reading; this is the only Location-affecting evidence found. tier=high/independent=true applies to the value that IS supported (the Texas endpoint); the Start-side location question is a CONCERN, not a sourced replacement value.

Journal Record: photo caption and body text repeatedly identify the project as 'Enable Midstream Partners' Wildcat pipeline project' / 'Enable's Wildcat.' Enable Midstream Partners, LP's own 10-Q describes it as 'The Partnership[']s' [Enable's] project, entering into agreements as the developer/owner. Continental Resources is named throughout as the ANCHOR SHIPPER/customer only, never as an owner or co-owner. Two distinct publishers (independent newspaper + Enable's own SEC filing, corroborated further by Continental's own SEC filing describing itself only as a shipper) agree Enable Midstream Partners LP is the sole developer/owner, matching Owner1=Enable Midstream Partners LP / Owner1%=100.00%. tier=high, independent=true. CONCERN (do not change the value; flagging for Update): Enable Midstream Partners, LP was acquired by Energy Transfer LP in a merger that closed February 2021 (SEC filings: Energy Transfer LP 8-K 0001193125-21-045834 and Form 425 0001193125-21-045839, both filed 2021-02-17, describing the Enable-Energy Transfer merger agreement). If GEM's Owner1 field is meant to reflect CURRENT ownership rather than ownership at the time the pipeline was built, 'Enable Midstream Partners LP' may now be a stale/superseded entity name (successor: Energy Transfer LP, or an Energy Transfer subsidiary). This is a corporate-ownership-history question or a stale-owner question, not a citation problem, so the value is left as staged -- flagging for a researcher to confirm current ownership and update if warranted.
